test_total does not fail. I ran the tests: test_plain and test_total pass. The one failure is test_half_cent_rounds_up.

Test run (python -m pytest -q): 2 passed, 1 failed.
FAILED test_cart.py::test_half_cent_rounds_up - assert 959 == 960

Why that test fails:
cart.total ends with int(subtotal * (1 - discount_percent / 100)). int() cuts off the fraction, it does not round.
- test_total: 399 * 0.9 = 359.1, int gives 359. The test wants 359, so it passes by luck of truncation.
- test_half_cent_rounds_up: 1010 * 0.95 = 959.5, int gives 959. The test wants 960, so it fails.
This matches the TODO line "customers see totals one cent short".

A likely fix (not applied; this was a question, so I changed no code): round half up in whole cents, for example with integer math:
    discounted = subtotal * (100 - discount_percent)
    return (discounted + 50) // 100
This gives 359 and 960 and avoids float error. Note that Python's round() uses banker's rounding (round(959.5) is 960, but round(958.5) is 958), so it is not half up in every case.
